column2: On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; and if he cannot, then with his heart—and that is the weakest of faith.” Reported by Muslim.
This hadith sets out the degrees of opposing evil: whoever is able to change it by hand is bound to do so. This applies to the ruler and his deputies in areas of general authority,
and also to the head of a household over the members of his household in areas of particular authority. “Seeing” evil may mean seeing with the eyes,
or, more broadly, both seeing it and knowing of it. If he is not one of those who can change it by hand, he moves on to changing it by the tongue, if he is able to;
otherwise what remains for him is changing it with the heart, which is the weakest of faith. Changing evil with the heart means hating the evil and having one's heart affected by it.
There is no contradiction between the command in this hadith to change evil and the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:

“O you who believe, upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves. Those who have gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided” [al-Māʾidah 5:105]. Its meaning is: when you have done what is required of you in enjoining good and forbidding evil,
you have fulfilled your duty, and after that the misguidance of those who go astray will not harm you when you are guided.

Our shaykh, Shaykh Muḥammad al-Amīn al-Shinqīṭī (may Allah have mercy on him), has excellent and thorough discussions of the issues of enjoining good and forbidding evil in his book Aḍwāʾ al-Bayān, in his treatment of this verse, and they are well worth consulting.
Enjoining good and forbidding evil is obligatory, and by it people and lands are set right.
Changing evil is in degrees; whoever is able to do any of them is bound to do so.
Faith varies in degree; some of it is strong, some weak and some weakest.
